chunks: We bear witness that there is no god but Allah, the One, without any partner for Him,
and that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger,
These two testimonies elevate the speech and raise the deed,
A scale upon which they are placed will not be light, nor will a scale from which they are removed become heavy.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of the two testimonies of faith in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) highlights the metaphysical potency of the Shahadatayn, noting that they serve as the primary mechanism for elevating both speech and action in the divine accounting. This concept underscores the Shia understanding that faith is not merely verbal but carries ontological weight that directly influences the balance of deeds on the Day of Judgment. The passage thus links the declaration of Tawhid and Nabuwwah to the practical reality of spiritual accountability.
